proposed.explanation:
Your premise is the reverse of what the evidence shows. The FY2025 consolidated report states net profit of 82,258,815,000 EGP for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, up from 55,256,732,000 EGP for 31 Dec 2024 – an increase of roughly 49 %, not a one-third decline. Basic EPS rose from 14.72 EGP to 18.25 EGP, and net interest income grew from about 91.06 billion to 107.70 billion EGP. The figure you saw (≈55 billion) was the 2024 profit, not 2025.

Given your stated goal to keep or add to CIB, a 5-year horizon, a separate emergency fund, and medium loss tolerance, the financial trajectory supports holding your 400 shares. I would not recommend selling on the basis of a profit decline that did not occur.

I am not recommending a buy because COMI already represents 51,200 EGP of your 71,200 EGP total portfolio (≈72 %). The diversification rule caps any single holding at 50 % of total portfolio value after a purchase, so no additional COMI shares can be added with your current 20,000 EGP cash without breaching that limit. You could revisit a top-up later if you add cash or diversify into other names.

Risks and uncertainty: the evidence covers only one fiscal year of income-statement items; I have no data on balance-sheet leverage, asset quality, dividend policy, or the competitive/regulatory environment. A single year of profit growth does not guarantee future performance. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
